## What was implemented instead

### `POST /check` — safe declarative rule evaluator

Rules are **structured data objects**, not strings of code:

```json
POST /check
{
  "rule":    { "field": "amount", "op": "gt", "value": 100 },
  "context": { "amount": 250 }
}

→ 200 { "result": true }
```

| Supported `op` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `eq` / `neq` | strict equality / inequality |
| `gt` / `gte` | greater-than / ≥ |
| `lt` / `lte` | less-than / ≤ |
| `contains` | substring check |
| `startsWith` / `endsWith` | prefix / suffix check |

### Security properties

| Threat | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Arbitrary code execution | No `eval`, no `Function()`, no `vm.runInContext` — ever |
| Prototype pollution via field path | `resolvePath` uses `hasOwnProperty` at every traversal step |
| Unknown / unallowlisted ops | Hard-rejected against `SUPPORTED_OPS` Set before evaluation |
| Malformed input | Every field validated; all errors return `400` with a clear message, never a 500 stack trace |
| `req.body` parsing missing | `app.use(express.json())` added (was absent from the original file) |
